issues.description: Constructor for class Animal and the 'age' attribute are inconsistent across artifacts. Problem statement UML declares an Animal constructor with signature Animal(String, int) and an 'age' attribute (problem_statement.md shows the Animal UML with attributes name and age and the constructor Animal(String, int)). The template Main.java instantiates Seal, Pig, Goat with a single String argument (see commented lines creating Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")), implying constructors with a single String parameter. The solution implementation defines Animal with only a name field and a constructor public Animal(String name) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java). This mismatch leaves students uncertain whether to implement Animal and its subclasses with (String) or (String, int) constructors and whether to include an age attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/attribute specification consistent. Preferred fix: update the UML and problem text to remove the 'age' attribute and change the Animal constructor in the UML to Animal(String) so it matches the template Main.java examples and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if age is required pedagogically, update the template Main.java and the solution's Animal and subclass constructors to accept (String, int) and add the age field with getters/setters. Document the chosen design in the problem statement so students know which constructor signature to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement UML declares Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor signature Animal(String, int). The template usage (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) define Animal with only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and no age attribute. This mismatch between the UML/description (Animal(String, int) and 'age' attribute) and the actual code (Animal(String) with only 'name') creates confusion about the intended Animal constructor signature and attributes: the problem asks for a two-parameter constructor and an 'age' field, while the code and example usage expect a single-parameter constructor (name) only. Students may be unsure which constructor to implement and whether to add an 'age' field to subclasses, and tests or provided template code may not compile if they follow the UML instead of the template.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the Animal constructor/attributes consistent across artifacts. Two options:
1) Prefer the existing template/solution: Update the problem statement UML and description to remove the 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructor, documenting Animal(String) and only the 'name' attribute. This is the least invasive fix and aligns the UML with provided code and examples.
2) Or, if 'age' is required pedagogically: Update the template and solution to add a private int age field and change the constructor to public Animal(String name, int age), update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to accept and forward the age parameter, and modify Main and tests to pass an age. Choose option 1 unless the exercise explicitly intends to teach multiple-attribute constructors.
